stories.headline: [The Guardian] As a Ukrainian journalist, I’ve covered the US for 20 years. I find it increasingly shocking
stories.summary: Ukrainian journalist Victoria Roshchyna has expressed shock at the US, having covered the country for 20 years. Her comments come as Ukraine continues to face challenges, including the ongoing Russian invasion and corruption. Recently, a top Ukrainian commander was fired after images of malnourished soldiers on the frontline were posted on social media, highlighting the lack of food and water for troops. The situation in Ukraine remains dire, with the country under occupation and struggling with war and corruption. Roshchyna, a recipient of the 2022 Courage in Journalism Award, has reported extensively on the Russian invasion and the Siege of Mariupol, providing a unique perspective on the conflict. Her observations on the US come as the international community continues to grapple with the ongoing crisis in Ukraine.

stories.headline: [Human Rights Watch] EU Parliament Confirms That ‘Only Yes Means Yes’
stories.summary: The European Parliament adopted a resolution calling for consent to be the determining factor in rape legislation across the EU. The resolution, which passed with 447 votes in favor, 160 against, and 43 abstentions, urges the European Commission to make "only yes means yes" the standard for consent. This means that silence or lack of resistance would not be considered consent. The resolution aims to harmonize rape laws across EU member states, ensuring that victims are protected and perpetrators are held accountable. The European Commission is expected to take the resolution into consideration when proposing new legislation. The adoption of this resolution reflects the European Parliament's commitment to strengthening human rights and combating violence against women. The resolution is a significant step towards creating a more consistent and effective approach to addressing rape and sexual violence across the EU.

stories.headline: [Kyiv Post] Why Putin Wants a May 9 Ceasefire in Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine during a 90-minute phone call with US President Donald Trump. The ceasefire would coincide with the May 9 Russian holiday marking the end of World War II. According to Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov, Putin expressed readiness for a truce during the commemorations, suggesting it could serve as a step toward broader peace negotiations. The proposal comes as Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, vowed to target Russia's "shadow grain fleet" and its enablers, citing data showing over 850,000 metric tons of grain were exported from occupied areas between January and April. The ceasefire proposal aims to mark the defeat of Nazi Germany, a significant event in Russian history, and potentially pave the way for further peace talks. Putin initiated the call with Trump, their first conversation in some time.

stories.headline: [News.com.au] Christchurch shooter Brenton Tarrant’s appeal thrown out by NZ court
stories.summary: The New Zealand Court of Appeal has dismissed Brenton Tarrant's bid to appeal his conviction and sentence. Tarrant, the Australian gunman behind the 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks, pleaded guilty in 2020 to 51 counts of murder, 40 counts of attempted murder, and a terrorism charge. He was sentenced to life without parole, a first in New Zealand. Tarrant's appeal claimed harsh prison conditions, but the court rejected this argument. The decision means Tarrant will remain behind bars for life. The Christchurch attacks occurred in March 2019, resulting in the deaths of 51 people and injuring 40 others. Tarrant's guilty plea and subsequent sentencing were notable, as he initially intended to defend the charges. The court's dismissal of his appeal upholds the original conviction and sentence.

stories.headline: vivo Y31d arrives May 9 with 7200mAh BlueVolt battery
stories.summary: The vivo Y31d will be released on May 9, featuring a 7200mAh BlueVolt battery, the largest power cell from vivo to date. This battery technology is designed to deliver stable and reliable performance for heavy everyday use. The device guarantees six-year battery health, supported by a 25-dimension safety protection system, ensuring consistent performance over time. On a single charge, the vivo Y31d can deliver up to 11.8 hours of gameplay and 14.5 hours of navigation. The phone is designed for users who value long-lasting battery performance, durability, and smooth everyday usability. With its large capacity battery, the vivo Y31d aims to provide a reliable and long-lasting mobile experience. The device's battery durability and safety features make it a notable option for those seeking a well-rounded smartphone.

stories.headline: Meta's new AI glasses review: Stellar sound, sharp recording, subject none the wiser
stories.summary: Meta's new AI glasses feature a 12-megapixel camera, taking 3K photos and videos, with an LED indicator that blinks when capturing content. The glasses connect to music streaming services like Apple Music and Spotify, producing high-quality sound. They have Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, two speakers, and five microphones, allowing for voice commands and audio functions. The glasses are available in Ray-Ban and Oakley designs, with the entry-level model retailing for £299. They can display text messages and maps, but the more advanced Display glasses with embedded screens cost $799 and are currently only available in the US. The AI-powered glasses offer a unique experience, with potential to bring about a shift in wearable AI and augmented reality technology. They can also function as regular sunglasses when not in use, making them a practical accessory.

stories.headline: I used AI to code a personal trainer app in one weekend. I see why big apps fear the competition.
stories.summary: Business Insider's Lee Chong Ming built a custom personal trainer app in one weekend using AI. The app replaced multiple tools and made him question the value of big fitness platforms. Ming's experience highlights the potential of AI-powered app development, allowing individuals to create customized solutions that rival established brands. The app utilized open-source information and chatbot technology, similar to ChatGPT. Ming's experiment also sparked the idea for a "ParentGPT" app, which correlates internet information into a chatbot for parents. The ease of creating such apps raises concerns among big tech companies, as individuals can now develop competitive products quickly and efficiently. Ming's project demonstrates the capabilities of AI tools and their potential to disrupt traditional industries, including fitness and technology. The app's functionality and effectiveness were tested over two weeks, comparing AI workouts and guidance to human trainers.

stories.headline: I coded a Fitness App in a Weekend. Big Apps Beware.
stories.summary: Business Insider's Lee Chong Ming built a custom trainer app in a weekend, replacing multiple tools and raising questions about the value of big fitness platforms. This feat was achieved through "vibe-coding," a no-code workflow that allowed the app to be developed in just 48 hours. The app's creation highlights the potential for individuals to create functional apps quickly and easily, potentially disrupting the market for big fitness platforms. Similar instances have been reported, such as high schoolers building a calorie-counting app using AI technology. The ease and speed of app development are changing the landscape of the tech industry, with many turning to no-code workflows to bring their ideas to life. This trend is expected to continue, with more individuals and developers creating innovative apps in short periods of time.

stories.headline: Aljamain Sterling calls for UFC featherweight title shot
stories.summary: Aljamain Sterling, a former bantamweight champion, has called for a UFC featherweight title shot after his win at UFC Vegas 116. Sterling, who moved up to the featherweight division in 2024, challenged reigning champion Alexander Volkanovski and no. 1 contender Movsar Evloev. He stated, "Volkanovski, you know I'm coming," and demanded respect for his name, saying he's next in line for a title shot. If Volkanovski and Evloev face off, Sterling could be in line to fight the winner. Sterling expressed respect for Volkanovski but made it clear he's coming for the title, saying "give me my damn title shot." With his recent win, Sterling solidified his position as one of the best in the world and is now seeking a title opportunity in the featherweight division.

stories.headline: Liverpool have only one choice for next manager and it isn't Xabi Alonso
stories.summary: Liverpool's search for a new manager has led to contact with Xabi Alonso's agent, according to German reports. Alonso, currently managing Bayer Leverkusen, is a former Liverpool midfielder. Despite initial speculation, he is now a potential candidate to replace outgoing Jurgen Klopp. Alonso has also drawn interest from Bayern Munich, another of his former clubs. Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy believes Luis Enrique would be a good fit for the role, but Alonso appears to be a leading contender. Alonso recently made headlines for his playing return in a Champions League quarter-final, filling in for an injured Steven Gerrard. His managerial experience and Liverpool ties make him an attractive option for the club. Liverpool is expected to make a decision on their next manager this summer.

stories.headline: Crows' skipper Jordan Dawson ruled out for Showdown after attending brother's funeral
stories.summary: Adelaide Crows captain Jordan Dawson will miss Friday's Showdown against Port Adelaide after attending his brother's funeral. Dawson's brother, Jaryd, passed away on April 15, and the funeral was held in Robe, South Australia, on Wednesday. The Adelaide Crows staff and players attended the service to support their captain. Dawson had played his first match since his brother's death on Sunday, breaking down in tears and sharing hugs with Brisbane players after the game. The club is giving him all the time he needs to grieve, ruling him out of the upcoming game. The sudden death of Jaryd Dawson sent shockwaves through the community and the AFL world, with the initial search for him concluding with the confirmation of his passing.

stories.headline: Bolton Wanderers eye two targets against Luton Town Bolton Wanderers boss Steven Schumacher hopes to nip Luton Town's recent momentum in the bud and deny them a play-off sport this weekend
stories.summary: Bolton Wanderers face Luton Town in the final game of the EFL League One regular season. The match is crucial, with Bolton aiming to deny Luton a play-off spot and secure home advantage in the play-off semi-finals. Luton have recorded 20 wins, 11 draws, and 14 losses in 45 games, averaging 1.58 points per game. Bolton manager Steven Schumacher hopes to stop Luton's momentum and finish the season strongly. A win for Bolton would cement third or fourth place. The match will determine the potential route to Wembley for Bolton, who are already planning to strengthen their squad for next season. The game is set to take place at the Macron Stadium, with both teams vying for a strong finish to the season. Bolton's objectives are to win the game and secure a favorable position in the play-offs.

stories.headline: Delhi-Mumbai Expressway tragedy: 5 Devotees burnt alive as moving car catches fire near Alwar
stories.summary: A car carrying devotees from Vaishno Devi caught fire on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway in Rajasthan's Alwar district, resulting in the deaths of five people. The victims, who were from Madhya Pradesh, were burnt alive in the incident. The driver of the car managed to jump out to safety, but was seriously injured. The accident occurred as the group was returning from their pilgrimage to Vaishno Devi. The cause of the fire is not yet known. The incident has been reported by police in Rajasthan's Alwar district, with investigations underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

stories.headline: 10 dead in Bengaluru rains: Hailstorm, heavy winds unleash chaos in city; watch
stories.summary: At least 10 people have died in Bengaluru due to heavy rainfall and a hailstorm that hit the city. The storm caused severe waterlogging, with waist-deep water in several areas, including Richmond Town and Shanthinagar. A wall collapse at Bowring Hospital resulted in seven deaths. The city witnessed its highest-ever April rain, leading to flooding and chaos. The heavy winds and hailstorm also caused injuries, with nine people reported hurt. The sudden and intense rainfall turned the city's streets into flowing streams, catching residents off guard. The incident occurred ahead of a birthday celebration, claiming the life of a six-year-old girl among others. The city's infrastructure was severely impacted, leading to disruptions and loss of life.

stories.headline: 'Cartographic Inaccuracies': Nepal Airlines Apologises For Distorted Map Showing J&K In Pakistan
stories.summary: Nepal Airlines has apologized for displaying an incorrect map of India, showing Jammu and Kashmir as part of Pakistan. The airline referred to the mistake as a "cartographic inaccuracy" and issued a formal apology following international backlash. The incident involved a promotional graphic that incorrectly depicted the boundaries of Jammu and Kashmir. Nepal Airlines has begun an internal review of the matter. The error may impact the airline's expansion plans in India. The apology was issued by Nepal's national flag carrier, Nepal Airlines Corporation (NAC), after the distorted map sparked widespread criticism. The airline has acknowledged the mistake and is taking steps to correct it and prevent similar errors in the future. The incident has drawn attention to the sensitive issue of territorial boundaries and mapping in the region.

stories.headline: A SIR-marred turnout in West Bengal
stories.summary: West Bengal's assembly polls concluded with a record voter turnout of 92.6% in the second phase, making it the highest in the state's electoral history. The total state turnout is also the highest since Independence. Compared to the previous assembly polls, the voter turnout has increased, with Phase 1 and Phase 2 showing higher participation than five years ago. The state's turnout has surpassed the 2024 Lok Sabha polls and the 2011 state election, which had a turnout of 84.72%. This record surpasses even Assam's 85.38% turnout in the recent election cycle, where a special revision of rolls was held. The high voter turnout indicates strong participation in the West Bengal Assembly elections.

stories.headline: Could the UAE's exit from Opec lead to its split-up as an oil cartel? The odds seem against it With Gulf rifts widened by war, the UAE’s plan to quit Opec is clearly a blow to this powerful oil cartel. Its departure may reshape oil markets and geopolitics
stories.summary: The UAE has announced its exit from OPEC, a move that could reshape oil markets and geopolitics. The decision, citing "national interests," is seen as a blow to the powerful oil cartel, particularly amid widened Gulf rifts due to the war on Iran. The UAE's departure may raise questions about the cartel's future, but officials from other OPEC+ members do not expect an immediate exodus. The move is viewed as a win for Donald Trump, who has previously criticized OPEC for artificially inflating oil prices. The exit is set to take place next month and is seen as a significant development in the region, potentially straining relations with Saudi Arabia while potentially aligning with US interests. The shared economic interests of OPEC's members may help hold the cartel together despite the UAE's departure.

stories.headline: Forget peak oil, peak geopolitics will wean us off the stuff Australia's fuel security faces uncertainty as global oil supply shocks, like Tuapse drone strikes, highlight our reliance. Understand the future of our energy.
stories.summary: Australia's fuel security is facing uncertainty due to global oil supply shocks. Recent drone strikes on Russian oil facilities, such as Tuapse, have highlighted the country's reliance on imported oil. Ukraine's strike on Russian oil facilities in the Baltic Sea, which export 2% of global oil supplies, has also impacted the market. Energy Minister Chris Bowen has assured that Australia's supply of petrol and diesel will remain stable for the next few weeks. However, the country's long-term energy security is a concern. Global oil demand is being revised due to government initiatives to reduce fuel use and fuel shortages. The crude oil futures market is being closely monitored, with real-time price data and key metrics being tracked to navigate the market and understand the future of energy. Australia is reevaluating its energy assumptions amidst these geopolitical developments.

stories.headline: No other headlines are provided to select from, only two headlines are given
stories.summary: Charlie Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, was abruptly rushed out of the White House Correspondents' Dinner, visibly shaken and in tears, according to an eyewitness. The incident occurred during the annual event, which brings together journalists, politicians, and celebrities. The White House Correspondents' Dinner is a prominent gathering that often features high-profile guests and speeches. Erika Kirk's departure from the event was notable, given her late husband's prominence as a conservative commentator. The incident has sparked interest and coverage from various news outlets, including The Post, which is providing live updates on the event. Further details about the incident are not yet available, but it has already generated significant attention and discussion. The event continues to be covered by major news outlets, including CNN and ABC News.

stories.headline: 'BJP Has Seen Defeat For 40 Years. That's Why It Never Loses In Gujarat Today'
stories.summary: The BJP has seen defeat for 40 years in Gujarat, which has driven its discipline and hunger for victory. In contrast, the Congress, which governed for 40 uncontested years, lacked this drive. The BJP, led by Modi, is now trying to expand into regions where it has struggled. Recent elections have been a test of the party's ability to make inroads in these areas. The BJP has won several seats, including Bhander, Bamori, and Ashok Nagar, while the Congress has won seats like Morena, Biora, and Agar. The BJP-led central government also introduced a delimitation bill, which was criticized as an attempt at gerrymandering. The party's efforts to expand its reach are ongoing, with a focus on gaining a foothold in new regions. The elections have been closely watched, with the BJP seeking to maintain its strong performance.

stories.headline: Narendra Modi -- a man with deep and vital experience of Indian politics -- has seen the BJP lose many elections between 1975 and 2015, and with every defeat,
stories.summary: Narendra Modi, the incumbent Prime Minister of India, has extensive experience in Indian politics, having served as Chief Minister of Gujarat from 2001 to 2014. He led the BJP to a landslide victory in the 2014 general election, becoming Prime Minister. Prior to this, the BJP suffered defeats, including the 2004 general election, which was attributed to the violence in Gujarat. Modi has been criticized for his relationship with Muslims and has faced allegations of corruption. The Enforcement Directorate has registered 5,422 cases under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, with only 23 convictions, mostly during Modi's premiership. The timing of raids on opposition leaders has raised questions about political motivations, with cases against some leaders being dropped after they defected to the BJP. Modi currently represents Varanasi in the Lok Sabha.

stories.headline: Congress Alleges BJP of Misusing Government Machinery in Gujarat Elections
stories.summary: The Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee alleged irregularities and misuse of administrative machinery in the local body election process. The party claimed that the ruling BJP was behind the withdrawals of 1,663 candidates, citing threats, monetary inducements, and offers of positions. The Congress also alleged a nexus between the BJP and the Aam Aadmi Party. The election results showed the BJP winning 59.36% of the vote in corporations, followed by the Congress at 26.46% and the AAP at 10.27%. The Leader of the Opposition criticized the BJP, accusing them of cheating the youth of Gujarat through paper leaks and other means. The allegations come amid the BJP's strong performance in the local body elections, with the party securing its best results in corporations.

stories.headline: Gujarat Polls: BJP and Congress Engage in War of Words Over Development and Governance
stories.summary: The BJP and Congress are engaged in a war of words over development and governance in the run-up to the Gujarat polls. Congress MP Anand Sharma criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi, calling him "less literate in economics." The BJP is confident of maintaining its winning streak in Kutch district, while the Congress is campaigning in rural areas. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has entered the fray, setting the stage for a three-cornered fight. In the recent local body polls, the AAP emerged as the second biggest party in the Surat Municipal Corporation, replacing the Congress. The BJP won a record 156 seats in the 2022 assembly elections, while the Congress's tally fell to 17 seats, its lowest in three decades. Counting is currently underway for the local body polls, with the BJP, Congress, and AAP in a key contest.

stories.headline: Stock Market Highlights, Apr 30:: Sensex, Nifty close in red as market breadth turns sharply negative Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights: Indian benchmark indices ended sharply lower on Thursday amid heightened volatility driven by surging crude oil
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices ended sharply lower on Thursday, with the BSE Sensex falling 582.86 points to close at 76,913.50. The decline was driven by surging crude oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions. Brent crude surged to $126, contributing to the market volatility. The Nifty 50 also closed in the red, with the market breadth turning sharply negative. The rupee fell against the US dollar, adding to the downward pressure on the market. The Sensex had earlier tanked over 1,000 points as crude oil prices rose, with markets opening in deep red due to the surge in Brent crude to $120. The decline marked a reversal from the previous week's winning streak, with the Sensex and Nifty 50 slipping in early trade on Monday. The market closed with a bearish note, reflecting the impact of global geopolitical tensions and rising oil prices.

stories.headline: Why is market falling today? Sensex slumps over 800 points, Nifty below 24,000; 8 key factors Indian stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Thursday. The Sensex and Nifty saw significant drops, erasing substantial market capitalization. This selloff
stories.summary: Indian stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Thursday, with the Sensex slumping over 800 points and the Nifty falling below 24,000. The selloff was broad-based, affecting smallcap and midcap stocks, and erasing substantial market capitalization. The Sensex declined to near the 76,800 mark, while the Nifty 50 slipped below the 24,000 level, a drop of over 0.7% for both indices. Soaring oil prices, a record low for the rupee, and global tensions were among the key factors driving the decline. The rupee hit 94.11, further impacting investor sentiment. The market downturn was significant, with the Sensex crashing over 1,100 points at one point, and the Nifty 50 going below 23,800. Eight key factors contributed to the decline, including global tensions and a weak rupee.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Today: Sensex, Nifty50 in Red as Oil Price Surge above $120 per Barrel Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty experienced a significant slump in early trade, driven by a sharp surge in crude oil prices above USD 120 per barrel,
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty slumped in early trade on Thursday, driven by a sharp surge in crude oil prices. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, rose over 4% to trade at $122.8 per barrel, above $120 per barrel. The 30-share BSE Sensex tumbled 821.79 points to 76,674.57, while the Nifty50 also declined. The surge in oil prices is attributed to US-Iran tensions, raising supply disruption fears. This has increased fiscal pressure on India, contributing to the decline in stock markets. Weak global trends and foreign fund outflows also played a role in the slump. The rise in oil prices has significant implications for India, given its reliance on crude oil imports. The stock markets are closely watching the developments, with investors concerned about the potential impact on the economy.

stories.headline: Stock Market LIVE: GIFT Nifty signals negative open; Asia markets fall; Brent crude above $121 Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates Thursday: The GIFT Nifty signalled a negative open for Nifty50 amid losses in global equities
stories.summary: The GIFT Nifty signaled a negative open for Nifty50, indicating a potential decline in the Indian stock market. This comes amid losses in global equities, with Asia markets also experiencing a downturn. Nifty futures traded 40 points lower at 25,990, hinting at a negative start for the domestic market. The decline is likely influenced by the surge in Brent crude prices, which have risen above $121. Global stock markets are also under pressure, with US stocks and crypto markets experiencing volatility. The negative trend in global markets is expected to impact the Indian stock market, with the Sensex and Nifty50 likely to open in the red. Investors are closely watching the market developments, with the GIFT Nifty serving as an indicator for the NSE's benchmark index NIFTY 50.

stories.headline: Oil price hits highest since 2022 after report Trump to be briefed on new Iran options
stories.summary: Oil prices have surged to their highest level since 2022, with Brent crude rising nearly 7% to over $126 per barrel. The increase comes after a report stated that the US military is preparing to brief President Donald Trump on new plans for potential action against Iran. This development has led to a significant jump in oil prices in Asia, with Brent crude reaching its highest level since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The price surge is also attributed to stalled US-Iran talks and potential plans to extend the blockade of Iranian ports. As a result, oil prices have briefly reached $126 per barrel, marking the highest level since the start of the Iran war and the highest since 2022. Iran has also announced fuel rationing amidst the rising tensions.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Soar as Iran Standoff Shows No End in Sight
stories.summary: Oil prices have surged to a new wartime high as the standoff between the US and Iran shows no signs of ending. The US naval blockade of Iran's ports will continue until Tehran abandons its nuclear program, according to President Trump. The ongoing conflict, now in its 60th day, has led to fears of a long-term supply disruption, driving oil prices up. Brent crude rose nearly 6% to $77 a barrel on Monday, before slightly falling back. The escalation has also impacted stock markets, with London's FTSE 100 down 1.2% at 10,780 points. Analysts warn that negotiations are stalled, and the US may escalate its actions to push for a better deal, suggesting no end to the conflict is in sight. This has resulted in soaring oil prices and inflation, with no clear resolution on the horizon.

stories.headline: Rising Fuel Prices Could Force Excruciating Choices on Economic Policies
stories.summary: The effective closing of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for fuel and other commodities off Iran's southern coast, has sharply increased energy prices. This development is expected to force difficult choices on economic policies. Economists and lawmakers are closely watching for signs of how central banks will respond to jumps in inflation. A recent two-week ceasefire in Iran led to a rally in global stock markets and a plunge in crude oil prices. However, there are concerns that long-lasting damage to the economy has already been set in motion. Rising fuel prices, which began before Russia's invasion of Ukraine, are expected to continue affecting people's finances, with the president's policies also contributing to the surge in fuel prices. The situation is being closely monitored for its potential impact on economic policies and inflation.

stories.headline: HUL Q4 Results: Stock falls nearly 4%; Management sticks to FY27 being than FY26 stance
stories.summary: Hindustan Unilever (HUL) reported a 16% increase in net profit for Q4, with a turnover of over ₹60,000 crore for FY25. The company achieved 2% underlying sales growth and 5% EPS growth, despite facing challenges due to a weaker product mix. HUL's management expects FY27 to be better than FY26. However, the company's stock fell nearly 4% following the announcement. Meanwhile, Coal India reported a 2% decline in coal production to 768.19 MT in FY26, with offtake down at 744.88 MT. Foreign Institutional Investors' continuous selling has also contributed to the market decline, with Nifty falling below 23,000. Other companies, including UltraTech Cement, are scheduled to release their earnings, which may impact the market further.

stories.headline: Elon Musk contradicts bold AGI claims, tells court Tesla isn’t working on it
stories.summary: Elon Musk testified in a California court that Tesla is not currently pursuing artificial general intelligence (AGI), contradicting his recent public claims. The testimony was part of his lawsuit against OpenAI, which hinges on profit cap distinctions. Musk had previously stated that Tesla was working towards AGI using robotics, real-world driving data, and computing strength, with potential collaboration with xAI to reach a breakthrough by 2026. However, in court, he clarified that Tesla is not actively pursuing AGI. The lawsuit also involves allegations that OpenAI's leaders secretly planned to convert the company to a for-profit corporation with backing from Microsoft, which exclusively licenses OpenAI's flagship product. Musk's contradictory statements raise questions about his strategy, credibility, and the future of AI competition. The case is ongoing, with implications for the development and commercialization of AI technology.

stories.headline: Anthropic Considering Funding Offers at Over $900 Billion Value
stories.summary: Anthropic PBC is considering a new funding round that would value the artificial intelligence developer at over $900 billion. This potential valuation exceeds previous proposals of $800 billion or more, which the company had resisted. According to people familiar with the matter, this funding round could make Anthropic the world's most valuable AI startup, surpassing its rival OpenAI. The valuation is based on offers from investors, and the company is weighing its options. If successful, the funding round would be a significant milestone for Anthropic, solidifying its position in the rapidly growing AI industry. The company's consideration of the funding offers marks a shift from its previous stance, indicating a potential change in its growth strategy.

stories.headline: Anxiety, resentment around AI spur violence against tech's figureheads
stories.summary: Proponents of artificial intelligence (AI) have been targeted in violent acts, reflecting growing public resentment and existential dread around the technology. Behavioral scientist Lily Jampol notes that "AI anxiety is real" and tied to uncertainty due to rapid developments. Workers are concerned about irresponsible AI implementation by their organizations. The incidents highlight a backlash against AI advocates, fueled by fears about the technology's impact. As AI continues to advance, concerns about job displacement, ethics, and accountability are escalating tensions. The violence against AI proponents is a disturbing manifestation of these anxieties, underscoring the need for responsible AI development and public engagement to address the concerns and uncertainties surrounding this emerging technology.

stories.headline: Families of Canada school shooting victims sue OpenAI over shooter's use of ChatGPT
stories.summary: Families of victims of a school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, Canada, are suing OpenAI in US federal court. The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI failed to alert police to the shooter's alarming interactions with ChatGPT. The shooting, carried out by 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar, is among the deadliest in Canadian history. Van Rootselaar used a long gun and a modified handgun to attack the local secondary school. The families claim that OpenAI prioritized "profit over lives" by not reporting the shooter's disturbing conversations with the chatbot to authorities. The lawsuit seeks to hold OpenAI responsible for its alleged failure to act on the shooter's violent and concerning interactions with ChatGPT. The case is being heard in a US federal court, with the families seeking accountability from the artificial intelligence company.
